To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
South Korea and African countries are not converging in terms of KE, and that there is a need to develop KE catch up strategies.

South Korea and African countries are at different stages in terms of KE development; KE development in South Korea was accelerated by assimilation of relatively obsolete technological know-how from developed nations; and African countries need to adopt a KE catch up strategy based on assimilating and adapting relatively obsolete technology from more advanced countries.
South Korea and African countries have different KE profiles, which are based on the following: South Korea has a high KE profile, whereas African countries have a low KE profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of institutions and incentives in the context of KE.
the extent to which African nations can emulate South Korea’s KE catch up strategies in the context of the challenges of globalisation and the emergence of a knowledge economy in Africa.
how African countries can catch up with South Korea in the KE and how South Korea can continue to lead in the KE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KE gap between the frontier country and the laggard countries is a result of a complex interaction of human capital, knowledge diffusion and economic incentives.
South Korea has a more developed KE than most African countries and that the latter can learn from South Korea in the areas of KE.
African countries should adopt South Korea’s knowledge economy catch up strategy, which is based on human capital, institutions, economic incentives and knowledge diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

African countries can catch up with South Korea by adopting a strategy that is based on the following: (i) a focus on the development of human capital, (ii) an emphasis on the diffusion and absorption of knowledge from more advanced nations, (iii) an emphasis on institutions that are conducive to the development of the KE, (iv) an emphasis on economic incentives that encourage the diffusion and absorption knowledge and the development of KE.
African countries can learn from South Korea’s KE catch up strategies.
African countries should adopt a pragmatic approach in their KE catch up strategy by adapting and assimilating knowledge and technologies from advanced countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KE gaps between South Korea and African countries are wide and that KE catch up strategies should focus on the creation, diffusion and application of knowledge.
the KE gap between South Korea and African countries is substantial, and this gap is not expected to close any time soon.
the African countries should focus on human capital development, knowledge creation and diffusion, institutional development, economic incentives and policies to catch up in the knowledge economy.
